PullRequest.Title: SCM Graph - truncate long reference names in the history item hover
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #235620

## Repro steps

1. Create a git repository with two commits.
2. On the latest commit, create a branch and a tag with ~120 character names, e.g. `git branch feature/a-very-long-branch-name-that-keeps-going-and-going-to-check-how-the-scm-graph-hover-handles-long-refs` and `git tag release/2026.11.14-a-very-long-tag-name-that-also-keeps-going-to-check-how-the-scm-graph-hover-renders-it`.
3. Open the folder, open the Source Control view, and hover the latest commit in the Graph view.
4. 🐛 The long reference names wrap inside their badges: the pill-shaped badges turn into full-width, two-line rounded blocks (as in the issue screenshot).

## Root cause

`toHistoryItemHoverContent` (`scmHistory.ts`) injects the references into the hover as inline `<span>` badges. In `scm.css` the references paragraph is a wrapping flex container, so each badge is a flex item that wraps its text when the name is wider than the hover. The markdown sanitizer only allows color, background, `display:inline-block`, and `border-radius` in inline styles, so the badge layout has to come from `scm.css`.

## Fix

- `scmHistory.ts`/`scm.css`: the rendered references section is marked with a `history-item-hover-references` class (instead of being targeted by its position, which missed hovers without a short statistics section, e.g. empty commits). The reference badges in it stay on a single line (`white-space: nowrap`), are capped at the hover width (`max-width: 100%`), and long names end with an ellipsis (`overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`). Short names render exactly as before.
- `scmHistory.ts`: each badge gets a `title` with the full reference name, so a truncated name can still be read. The name is HTML-attribute encoded, and `$` is encoded as well so theme-icon rendering (which runs on the rendered HTML string) cannot rewrite `$(...)` sequences inside the attribute.

## Validation

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm run typecheck-client` | ✅ passed |
| `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmHistory.ts` | ✅ passed |
| `pnpm run stylelint src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/media/scm.css` | ✅ passed (no errors) |
| `node build/hygiene.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/media/scm.css src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmHistory.ts` | ✅ passed |
| `pnpm run build-fast` + `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --dev <scenario>` (with fix) | ✅ all 3 steps passed |
| Same scenario for an empty commit (hover without the short statistics section) | ✅ all 3 steps passed |
| Same scenario with the fix reverted | ❌ failed as expected: both long badges are 38px tall vs 19px for `main`, and no badge exposes the full name |

The UI scenario (validate-ui-scenario harness, Code OSS dev build, throwaway profile, scratch repo with a `main` branch plus a ~120 character branch and tag on the same commit) opens the Graph, hovers the commit, and asserts on the DOM that every reference badge is a single line (same height as the `main` badge), fits inside the hover, and has the full reference name as its `title`.

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots and a side-by-side recording (before on the left, after on the right, labelled) are available; they can be attached to this PR (media can't be uploaded from the CLI).

- **Before:** the `main` badge is a 19px pill, but the long branch and tag badges wrap onto two lines and become full-width 38px rounded blocks (the hover is 222px tall).
- **After:** all three badges are 19px single-line pills. The long branch and tag names end with an ellipsis at the hover's width, the full name shows as the badge tooltip, and the hover shrinks to 184px tall. Short names are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading and rendering Source Control Graph rows, including scrolling/recycling rows that have branch or tag references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The graph first awaits history-provider work (workbench-to-extension-host IPC and the Git provider's log operation), then builds view models and synchronously renders visible virtual-tree rows. The diff adds HTML-attribute encoding plus a dollar-sign replacement for each rendered reference name and one class toggle per rendered tooltip section on the UI-thread row-render path; it does not add work before provider completion or add a new boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and serialize a page of SCM history items between the workbench and extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per requested graph page; load-more may request additional pages, with no per-reference IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider IPC and history-item serialization occurred before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The page must arrive before its rows can render. The changed title encoding/class assignment happens afterward and does not increase IPC payload or request count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the Git history log used to populate a graph page
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Git log operation per provider page request, serving all commits and references returned in that page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Git log operation populated each requested history page before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The log must complete before provider items are returned; the diff neither adds nor reschedules it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve optional commit avatars through registered history-item detail providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched avatar query for the commits in a provider result; provider-specific cache/network behavior is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same optional avatar-provider resolution was already on graph-page loading's critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Avatar resolution is awaited before history items cross IPC, but the reviewed changes occur only during later row rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Provider pages are configured from 1 to 1000 items; the Git provider defaults to 50 when no limit is supplied. UI work scales with the effective number of references and total reference-name characters among rows actually rendered/recycled by the virtualized tree. Reference labels and Markdown/DOM nodes were already constructed per reference before the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The provider request is awaited as one logical page request; its Git log and subsequent provider steps are sequenced. Row rendering and the added string scans/class toggles execute synchronously on the UI thread for virtualized rows, not as a concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fetched history pages are retained in repository view-model state, but hover DOM is rebuilt when a row template is rendered. The added title attribute is retained only with that row's existing rendered hover content and is released through elementDisposables when the row is recycled; no cache key, miss behavior, negative cache, or coalescing behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous work and lifecycle: the changed code is called directly from renderElement, loops over historyItem.references, and row disposables are cleared on recycling. High confidence that no expensive boundary cardinality changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repositories can place many references on one commit, but Git reference names are short relative to the already-existing per-reference Markdown sanitization and DOM construction. Exact UI-thread duration varies with visible rows and reference density; the diff adds only two linear string scans and a bounded class mutation, with no evidence of a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added CPU/allocation is linear in reference-name bytes but small relative to the pre-existing per-reference Markdown and DOM rendering, remains bounded by virtualized row lifetime, and does not alter provider IPC, Git subprocess, network work, concurrency, or cache behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Displaying and interacting with a history-item hover containing long reference names
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover content has already been constructed during row rendering. Showing the delayed hover attaches/displays that content and browser style/layout computes flex wrapping, max width, clipping, and ellipsis. The added native title is consulted only when the user points at a badge and performs no repository or extension-host work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Layout scales with the references on the single hovered commit. The patch keeps one existing span per reference and adds CSS properties/title text rather than adding DOM nodes; long labels no longer create additional wrapped lines.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover display and layout run on the single UI thread. Hover lifecycle grouping allows one SCM history-item hover group rather than creating parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pre-rendered hover content lives with the virtualized row and is disposed when the row is recycled. There is no cold/warm remote cache or negative cache on hover display, and the diff adds no persistent map or retained-key collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the CSS applies only beneath .monaco-hover.history-item-hover, and the TypeScript change marks only the injected reference Markdown section. The path contains DOM/style work but no changed IPC, subprocess, filesystem, database, or network call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/layout cost depends on badge count and hover width, but the new selectors are scoped to the one visible history hover and add ordinary overflow/ellipsis properties. No forced geometry read, repeated relayout loop, filter, or animation is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The patch changes the layout result for long labels without increasing node count or triggering a repeated layout mechanism; it likely reduces hover height for long names and has no new expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced eager row rendering, hover display/layout, row disposal, provider IPC, Git history retrieval, optional avatar resolution, scaling, cache behavior, and concurrency. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
